column1: # Every file in the MSVC bundled GStreamer runtime, and the upstream project it comes from.
# The MinGW flavour is licenses/third-party/COMPONENTS.tsv; this is the same ledger for the
# MSVC flavour. Both are read the same way -- ThirdPartyLicenseTests checks every shipped
# binary against a license text under licenses/third-party/, and
# .github/workflows/release.yml compares the matching publish directory against the matching
# ledger -- an exact match (missing AND extra), because a count floor cannot catch extra
# Generated from the runtime tree, not written by hand. Plugin-to-subproject attribution
# attribution comes from where each library is built in the GStreamer 1.28.6 tree.
# The MSVC build names the same libraries WITHOUT the 'lib' prefix, so no path here matches
# a path in the MinGW ledger. Two differences are real, not just naming:
#   * no libgcc_s_seh-1.dll / libstdc++-6.dll / libwinpthread-1.dll -- the MSVC build uses
#     the Microsoft C/C++ runtime instead, which is NOT bundled: msvcp140.dll,
#     vcruntime140.dll and vcruntime140_1.dll resolve outside the tree, so this flavour
#     requires the VC++ redistributable on the user's machine (THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)
#   * gstwinrt-1.0-0.dll is here and not in the MinGW ledger -- it is what makes Windows
#     Graphics Capture available, and therefore what makes d3d12screencapturesrc carry the
# lib/gstreamer-1.0/gstd3d12.dll is the one file that is NOT an upstream binary: it is
# built from the same 1.28.6 sources plus patches/gst-plugins-bad-1.28.6-d3d12-monochrome-
# cursor.patch. Project stays gst-plugins-bad -- the licence is unchanged. See
# Columns (tab separated): Path (relative to runtimes/win-x64), Project.
